problem_markdown: For pairwise coprime positive integers $a,b,c$, prove that $2abc-ab-bc-ca$ is the largest integer not expressible as $xbc+yca+zab$ with nonnegative integers $x,y,z$.
solutions_markdown:
Set $F=2abc-ab-bc-ca$. If $F=xbc+yca+zab$, reduction modulo $a,b,c$ gives $x\equiv-1\pmod a$, $y\equiv-1\pmod b$, $z\equiv-1\pmod c$. Nonnegativity then implies
$$xbc+yca+zab\ge(a-1)bc+(b-1)ca+(c-1)ab=F+abc>F,$$
a contradiction.

Now take any integer $N>F$. Choose $0\le x<a$, $0\le y<b$, $0\le z<c$ such that $xbc\equiv N\pmod a$, $yca\equiv N\pmod b$, $zab\equiv N\pmod c$. Pairwise coprimality makes these choices possible. For $S=xbc+yca+zab$, the difference $N-S$ is divisible by $abc$. Since $S\le F+abc$ and $N>F$, we have $N-S>-abc$. Thus $N-S=tabc$ for an integer $t\ge0$, and $N=(x+ta)bc+yca+zab$ is represented. The argument also covers parameters equal to one.
